newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks seen underpinned, eye Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks seen underpinned, eye Greenspan.

text.p: Singapore stocks were seen range-bound on Tuesday ahead of Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to Congress later in the day, dealers said.
"It will be watched for potential impact on Wall Street," said a dealer with a local institution.
However, domestic economic factors and regional currency developments will still be the dominant market movers.
Dealers said the higher-than-expected 8.8 percent growth in Singapore's June non-oil exports would continue to underpin the market but gains could be capped by potential profit-taking.

"The Trade Development Board figures confirmed what the market already knew. I won't be surprised if some are prompted to take profit. You know, buy on rumours and sell on fact," a dealer with a local firm said.
On Monday, the Straits Times Industrials Index ended 26.52 points up at 1,950.75, while Wall Street closed up 16 points at 7,907.
